# Pokémon Origin HeartGold English translation

> The official site of the Origin HeartGold English translation. Patches are published only on our GitHub releases. Origin HeartGold (起源心金) v4.0.3 is a Chinese fan game built on Pokémon HeartGold, by 雁南飞TB (Yannanfei TB), with v4 by Alex. The English translation is a free patch for your own Pokémon HeartGold Version (USA) ROM (CRC32 C180A0E9); no ROMs are provided. The current English patch is v1.0.0-rc8, released 13 October 2026. This site also has a walkthrough (quest guide), a Pokédex and reference pages for locations, items, moves, abilities, TMs and trainers.

© 2026 Origin HeartGold English translation team. The guide and website text is all rights reserved: linking to any page and short quotes with a link back are welcome. Facts and game data are not ours to claim. Full terms: https://github.com/originheartgold/origin-heart-gold-EN-translation/blob/main/LICENSE-GUIDE

Official links:

- Website: https://originheartgold.github.io/
- Download and patch in the browser: https://originheartgold.github.io/patch/
- GitHub releases (the only place patches are published): https://github.com/originheartgold/origin-heart-gold-EN-translation/releases
- Latest release notes: https://github.com/originheartgold/origin-heart-gold-EN-translation/releases/tag/v1.0.0-rc8
- GitHub repository: https://github.com/originheartgold/origin-heart-gold-EN-translation
- Discord (official community): https://discord.gg/sQY2udrQS

## Download the English patch

Source: https://originheartgold.github.io/patch/

> **Content warning: mature audiences:** 
This fan game contains strong language, sexual themes and innuendo, violence, death, and dark humour. It is intended for mature audiences and is not suitable for children.

**The official site of the Origin HeartGold English translation. Patches are published only on our GitHub releases.** Current English patch: **v1.0.0-rc8**, released 13 October 2026 ([release notes](https://github.com/originheartgold/origin-heart-gold-EN-translation/releases/tag/v1.0.0-rc8), [all changes](https://originheartgold.github.io/changelog/)).

Drop your own **Pokémon HeartGold Version (USA)** file below, as a `.nds` or a `.zip`, and you get Origin HeartGold (起源心金) v4.0.3 in English back.
The page checks your file, downloads the patch published with this site and applies it for you. You don't need to download the patch, find a patching tool or unzip anything.

> **Bring your own game:** 
No ROMs are provided here, ever. Dump your own HeartGold (USA) cartridge first.
The European, Japanese and Korean versions won't work, and neither will a file that's already patched or trimmed: the page tells you if your file is one of those.

### Good to know

- **Nothing is uploaded.** Everything happens in your browser tab. Your file never leaves your device; the page only downloads the patch from this website.
- **Keep your original file.** The patcher makes a new file and never changes yours. You need the original again for every new version of the patch.
- **Checked twice.** The page only patches a clean HeartGold (USA) dump, CRC32 **C180A0E9**, and checks the finished game against the SHA-1 published with the release before it lets you save it.
- **Then play** the saved `.nds` in an emulator. The patch is tested in [melonDS](https://melonds.kuribo64.net/); other emulators haven't been tested. Playing on a real DS, DSi or 3DS? See [the FAQ](https://originheartgold.github.io/faq/#can-i-play-on-a-real-ds-dsi-or-3ds).
  More help is on the [How to use this guide](https://originheartgold.github.io/about/#what-you-need-to-play) page.

### What's new in rc8

Version **v1.0.0-rc8** (4.0.3-RC8 inside the game) is a release candidate. It is not yet tested on real hardware. Earlier releases are on the [changelog](https://originheartgold.github.io/changelog/); the full technical list is in the changelog on [GitHub](https://github.com/originheartgold/origin-heart-gold-EN-translation).

- **Freezes fixed:** stepping under the arch in front of the stairs on Victory Road (reported on a real DS Lite), the weekday siblings' ribbon scene, the Pallet Town photographer when none of your Pokémon can fight, losing to Giovanni at the Mt. Silver hot spring, and scripted Double Battles when you have fewer than two Pokémon (such as the Department Store's 6F).
- **Money and quantities:** the Goldenrod fortune teller, the younger Haircut Brother and the S.S. Anne shop now check for the price they charge; the Game Corner's "500 coins" option gives 500 coins. Rewards of several items say how many you got ("Obtained Ultra Ball x2!").
- **Story fixes:** the Ilex Forest bug hunt can no longer set off the Forest of Time scenes early, the Cynthia romance scenes take the Snow Mail they ask for, Petilil holding a Black Belt evolves straight into Hisuian Lilligant, the Blackthorn tutor teaches Play Rough and the Saffron dojo tutor always teaches Volt Switch. The Ice Stone and the Dragon Scale can be used from the Bag again, so the Pokémon that evolve with them can evolve.
- **Names and sprites:** the player's name no longer shows up blank in dozens of lines, and 36 stationary overworld Pokémon are drawn as the species the text and cry name.
- **Battles:** fainting Pokémon cry again and moves that deal damage play the hit sound.
- **Difficulty settings:** ITEMS LIMITED is renamed **DEFAULT** and now follows the original hack's battle-item rules (Potions included); **ALL** still adds twenty more medicines. SHARE OFF no longer disables a held Exp. Share, and CAP, SHARE and ITEMS now also apply in story battles you can lose. See [Difficulty settings](https://originheartgold.github.io/difficulty/).
- **Text fixes:** the Route 21 Trainer's Lairon, the Celadon Skitty boy's "Fluffy Tail" and the Rock Tunnel tutor (who now names Pollen Puff, the move he teaches).

Fixes marked "Fixed in rc8" on the [Known issues](https://originheartgold.github.io/guide/known-issues/) page are the ones above.

### How it works

The page computes your file's CRC32 and SHA-1 (unpacking a `.zip` first with your browser's built-in decompression),
downloads the patch published with this website and applies it with
[xdelta3](https://github.com/jmacd/xdelta) compiled to WebAssembly by [xdelta-wasm](https://github.com/kotcrab/xdelta-wasm),
inside a background worker in your browser tab. Both are open source under the Apache License 2.0; see the [credits](https://originheartgold.github.io/about/#credits).

## FAQ

Source: https://originheartgold.github.io/faq/

The questions players ask most, with short answers and links to the full details.

### Stuck in the story?

The story often moves on only after you talk to the right person, sometimes someone you've already talked to. If Blue or Green tells you to "ask around", talk to everyone in town again, inside buildings too. These are the places where most players get stuck:

| Where you're stuck | What to do |
|---|---|
| Pewter City: Brock keeps leaving the Gym | Follow him to the north-east house, the museum (answer his siblings' quizzes) and the flower garden. [Finding Brock](https://originheartgold.github.io/guide/ch01-first-badge/#pewter-city-finding-brock-the-gym-leaders-errands) |
| Mt. Moon: guards block the way | [What opens the roadblock](https://originheartgold.github.io/guide/ch02-mt-moon/#mt-moon-what-opens-the-fake-guards-roadblock) |
| Vermilion City: "ask around town some more" | Talk to all six people involved, including Granny Kin right next to Lt. Surge at the construction site, then go back to Blue or your friend in the Pokémon Center. [The construction-site dispute](https://originheartgold.github.io/guide/ch05-vermilion-thunder/#vermilion-city-the-construction-site-dispute-choose-a-side) |
| Lavender Town: nothing happens at the Pokémon Tower | Go to Mr. Fuji's Pokémon House and talk to the Cubone. [Pokémon Tower](https://originheartgold.github.io/guide/ch07-rock-tunnel-lavender/#pok%C3%A9mon-tower-side-battles-and-extras) |
| Lavender Town: "I want to see you..." and you can't leave town | The Lavender curse: buy the fortune-teller's 10 Cleanse Tags and use them at an exit, then talk to the girl in the fortune-teller's house and answer No. [The girl who waits](https://originheartgold.github.io/guide/ch07-rock-tunnel-lavender/#route-10--lavender-town-the-girl-who-waits-the-lavender-curse) |
| Celadon City: where is Erika's Gloom? | [The stolen Gloom](https://originheartgold.github.io/guide/ch08-celadon/#celadon-city-the-stolen-gloom-story-chain-easy-to-get-stuck) |
| Celadon Rocket base: the Persian statue password | The password changes with the day of the week and the hour. [How to read it](https://originheartgold.github.io/guide/ch08-celadon/#celadon-rocket-warehouse-the-secret-passage-and-the-persian-statue-password) |
| Saffron City: a barrier blocks every gate | Talk to someone at the north, south and west gates, then go back to Sabrina at the east gate (Route 8). [Getting past the barrier](https://originheartgold.github.io/guide/ch11-saffron-takeover-marsh-badge/#saffron-city-takeover-getting-past-the-barrier-into-the-city) |

Some story choices only come once, like the [bomb on the S.S. Anne](https://originheartgold.github.io/guide/ch06-ss-anne/#ss-anne-defuse-the-bomb-or-the-ship-sinks-one-chance). Missable rewards are marked in the guide; [Known issues](https://originheartgold.github.io/guide/known-issues/) lists the ones that can close for good.

### Getting the game running

#### Is this the official site? Where do I get the patch?

Yes. This is the official site of the Origin HeartGold English translation. Patches are published only on our [GitHub releases](https://github.com/originheartgold/origin-heart-gold-EN-translation/releases). The [patch page](https://originheartgold.github.io/patch/) on this site uses the same patch and applies it in your browser. If another site offers the patch, it isn't from us: get it here or from GitHub, so you know it's the current, unmodified release. What changed in each version is on the [changelog](https://originheartgold.github.io/changelog/).

#### Where can I get help or talk to other players?

Join the official [Discord](https://discord.gg/sQY2udrQS) to ask questions and talk to other players. To report a mistake in the game or the guide, use the links at the bottom of every page or open an issue on [GitHub](https://github.com/originheartgold/origin-heart-gold-EN-translation/issues).

#### Which HeartGold do I need?

**Pokémon HeartGold Version (USA)**, a clean, untrimmed copy (CRC32 `C180A0E9`). European, Japanese, Korean and already-patched files won't work. The [patcher on this site](https://originheartgold.github.io/patch/) checks your file for you and accepts both `.nds` and `.zip`.

#### The patch fails: "not a VCDIFF input", "source file too short", "secondary decompressor" or "file too big"

Use the [patcher on this site](https://originheartgold.github.io/patch/): it handles zipped files and tells you what's wrong with your file. If you patch by hand, these errors usually mean one of these:

- **The two files are swapped.** Your HeartGold `.nds` is the source (original) file, the `.xdelta` is the patch.
- **A file is still zipped.** Unzip both first.
- **Wrong or modified HeartGold file.** Get a clean USA copy, not a "Rev 1", European or already-patched file.
- **The patching tool is too old.** Some tools, including Rom Patcher JS and some phone apps, can't read this patch. [xdelta-wasm](https://kotcrab.github.io/xdelta-wasm/) works.

#### Can someone send me the patched game?

No. Sharing ROMs isn't allowed, here or on the [Discord](https://discord.gg/sQY2udrQS). The patch is all you need, plus your own HeartGold (USA) file.

#### Which emulator should I use?

The translation was tested in [melonDS](https://melonds.kuribo64.net/). The automated checks for rc8, including the text speed setting, ran in DeSmuME; the freeze and battle fixes in rc8 were also checked in melonDS 1.1. There has been no full second-emulator pass for this build. Players also use DraStic, Lemuroid and others, but those aren't tested. For a real DS, DSi or 3DS, see the next question.

#### Can I play on a real DS, DSi or 3DS?

Yes, from rc6 on, but it hasn't been tested on a real console yet. The original Chinese hack has anti-piracy checks that make the game freeze after a while when it runs from a flashcart or loader on a real console (often when you open a menu or start a battle), even when it boots fine. The English patch now switches those checks off. On emulators nothing changes.

- **3DS and 2DS with TWiLight Menu++:** untested. Please try it and tell us how it goes. Update TWiLight Menu++ and nds-bootstrap to the newest versions. Select the game, press **Y** for its per-game settings and set **Run in: DSi mode** and **VRAM: DSi**.
- **DSi with TWiLight Menu++, DSPico, and DS or DS Lite flashcarts (R4 with Wood R4, YSMenu, AKAIO…):** untested. Please try it and tell us how it goes.
- **Don't add another anti-piracy patch.** The fix is built into the English patch. Don't apply a separate anti-piracy patch or an nds-bootstrap anti-piracy `.ips` file on top of it, and turn off your flashcart's own anti-piracy patching for this game if it has an option for that.

If it freezes, report it on the [Discord](https://discord.gg/sQY2udrQS) or on [GitHub](https://github.com/originheartgold/origin-heart-gold-EN-translation/issues) with:

1. your console, and the loader or flashcart with its version (for TWiLight Menu++, also the nds-bootstrap version);
2. the per-game settings you used (DS or DSi mode, CPU speed, VRAM);
3. the patch version;
4. where it froze and what you were doing, how long you had been playing since you switched it on, and how many Badges you have;
5. whether the screen went black or the picture froze;
6. if you use nds-bootstrap, a RAM dump: open its in-game menu with **L + Down + Select** and save a RAM dump (the [nds-bootstrap controls page](https://wiki.ds-homebrew.com/nds-bootstrap/controls) has the details), then attach `ramDump.bin` from the `_nds/nds-bootstrap` folder on your SD card.

Crashes in a story scene that also happen on an emulator come from the original hack, not your console: check [Known issues](https://originheartgold.github.io/guide/known-issues/) first.

#### How do I update to a new version without losing my progress?

1. Patch your **original** HeartGold (USA) file again with the new version. A patch can't be applied on top of an already-patched game.
2. **Save in game** before you switch. Emulator save states don't carry over between versions.
3. Give your save file the same name as the new game file (for example `Origin_HeartGold_EN.nds` and `Origin_HeartGold_EN.sav`), or import it in your emulator.

New versions of the translation don't change the save format, so your save keeps working.

#### The game crashes after Misty's Gyarados, when I open the Bag or a Pokémon's summary, or at the move reminder

You're on an old version of the patch (before rc4). The crashes after double-size shouts like Misty's and on the Bag and summary screens are fixed in the current release. Update as described above and keep your save. A freeze at Mr. Psychic's move reminder in Saffron City has also been reported; it didn't happen in our emulator tests of the current release. If it still happens to you, please [report it](https://originheartgold.github.io/contribute/) with a screenshot and the Pokémon you were teaching.

#### There are several English patches. Which one is this?

This site covers the English translation, which keeps the Chinese hack exactly as it was made. Other community patches, such as ones that add level caps or a hard mode, are shared on the [Discord](https://discord.gg/sQY2udrQS). This guide doesn't cover their changes. Each patch has to be applied to a clean HeartGold (USA) file; you can't stack them.

### Game settings and speed

#### Why does the game run fast, and slow down in towns?

The original Chinese hack runs the overworld at a higher speed (a "60 fps" feature). It's busier in towns with many characters on screen, so it feels slower there. It's part of the hack, not the translation. The released translation keeps this behavior. Make sure your emulator itself is set to normal (1×) speed.

#### Is there a text speed setting?

Yes. The Options screen has a seventh row, **TEXT SPEED**, with **NORMAL** and **FAST**. NORMAL is the original hack's text speed. FAST prints up to three letters per frame when the frame has room, and is never slower than NORMAL. New games start on FAST. If you load a save made before this setting existed, it shows NORMAL; change it in Options and save. MUSIC SPEED is still a separate option.

Text also prints faster in towns and on routes, at both settings. In those places the hack runs at 30 fps and used to print one letter every two frames; it now prints one letter per frame, as the original game does on FAST. A side effect is that some short pauses in those scenes are about half as long as in the Chinese hack.

Phone calls now wait for you to press A or B on every page, including right after a battle. Some other text shown right after a battle may still advance by itself, as in the original hack.

If you will go back to the Chinese hack or an older English patch with a save from this version, set TEXT SPEED to NORMAL and save first. Text speed shares a field that older versions use for MUSIC SPEED, and a FAST setting can show up there as an odd value.

Not everything has been checked with the setting: cutscenes, the intro and credits, the radio and TV, mail and the naming screen were not covered by our tests.

#### Why does Kanto play the Johto battle music?

Until you first set foot in Vermilion City (any way in, which also unlocks it as a Fly destination), wild and Trainer battles in Kanto use the Johto themes. From then on they switch to the Kanto themes. Gym Leader, rival and other special battle themes don't change. The rule comes from HeartGold, where you first reach Kanto by ship at Vermilion; the hack starts you in Kanto but kept it. The original Chinese game does the same.

#### Some moves have no sound. Is my game broken?

No. In the original hack these newer moves have no sound effect: Electro Ball, Soak, Flame Charge, Coil, Low Sweep, Acid Spray, Foul Play, Simple Beam, After You, Round, Echoed Voice, Chip Away, Clear Smog, Synchronoise and Venom Drench. Terrain Pulse has no animation at all. Opposing Pokémon don't cry when they faint, either (wild or a Trainer's). Moves from the original games, like Vine Whip, keep their sounds; if one of those is silent for you, check your emulator's audio settings.

#### Can I turn off the shared EXP, or set a level cap?

Yes, from rc7. The original hack has neither: your whole party shares EXP and EVs automatically ([details](https://originheartgold.github.io/mechanics/#automatic-exp-and-ev-sharing)). The English patch adds two optional settings on the second Options page: **SHARE** (turn it OFF so benched Pokémon get no EXP or EVs, except one holding an Exp. Share) and **CAP** (a level cap). They start at SHARE ON and CAP OFF, the original behaviour. A third setting, **ITEMS** (DEFAULT or ALL), controls which medicine you can use from the Bag in Trainer battles. Since rc8 the settings also apply in story battles you are allowed to lose, and SHARE OFF no longer switches off a held Exp. Share. The cap follows your Gym progress; see [Difficulty settings](https://originheartgold.github.io/difficulty/) for how to turn them on and when the cap goes up.

### Training your Pokémon

#### How do I see IVs and EVs?

Open a Pokémon's summary, go to the stats page and press **L**. More controls are on [Mechanics and controls](https://originheartgold.github.io/mechanics/#information-screen-controls).

#### Are shiny odds increased? What are the catch-chain thresholds?

**Yes, the verified wild-encounter code adds a boosted shiny check even without a chain.** That check starts at **1 in 4,096**, or **1 in 2,048** with the [Shiny Charm](https://originheartgold.github.io/items/shiny-charm/). The bonuses increase after **6, 10 and 20 completed catches** of the same species and form, and apply when the next encounter is generated.

| Completed catches | Extra shiny check: no charm | Extra shiny check: Shiny Charm |
|---|---:|---:|
| 0–5 | 1 in 4,096 | 1 in 2,048 |
| 6–9 | 49 / 65,536 (about 1 in 1,337) | 1 in 1,024 |
| 10–19 | 81 / 65,536 (about 1 in 809) | 97 / 65,536 (about 1 in 676) |
| 20+ | 113 / 65,536 (about 1 in 580) | 1 in 512 |

**These are the extra check's odds, not exact overall encounter odds.** The fractions count successful values out of the random number generator's 65,536 possible outputs. If that check fails, ordinary Pokémon generation can still produce a shiny; its interaction with the extra check has not been fully quantified. We therefore cannot yet give one exact combined rate for each tier. The Chain Logger's fractions differ slightly because it displays a rounded divisor rather than accounting for every successful random value.

The in-game range labels are also inaccurate at 10 and 20: use the thresholds above. There is no further increase beyond 20 catches in this check. See [capture chains](https://originheartgold.github.io/mechanics/#capture-chains) for chain resets, IV and Hidden Ability bonuses, and the encounter types verified so far. These rates should not be assumed for starters, gifts or Eggs.

#### Can I change natures and abilities?

Yes, in shops:

- **Mints** (change the nature's stat effect): $9,000 each at the Celadon Department Store 4F and the Goldenrod Department Store 1F. For example the [Adamant Mint](https://originheartgold.github.io/items/adamant-mint/).
- [Ability Capsule](https://originheartgold.github.io/items/ability-capsule/) ($25,000) and [Ability Patch](https://originheartgold.github.io/items/ability-patch/) ($50,000): Celadon Department Store 4F.
- **Hidden Abilities** also come from catch chains with the [Chain Logger](https://originheartgold.github.io/mechanics/#capture-chains).

#### Why do all my wild catches have the same nature?

Your first party Pokémon has the ability [Synchronize](https://originheartgold.github.io/abilities/synchronize/). In this hack Synchronize **always** passes its nature to wild Pokémon (in HeartGold it works half the time), including shinies. It counts even if that Pokémon has fainted. Synchronize Pokémon include Abra, Kadabra, Alakazam, Natu, Xatu, Espeon, Umbreon, Baltoy, Claydol, Munna and Musharna, and Ralts and Kirlia with their Hidden Ability. Put a Pokémon without Synchronize first for random natures, or lead with a Synchronize Pokémon of the nature you want. It also works in scripted battles with a single Pokémon, such as legendaries; gift Pokémon aren't affected.

#### How do I nickname a Pokémon I caught?

Wild catches don't ask for a nickname in this hack (gifts do). Visit the Name Rater in the north-east house of Viridian City.

#### How do I evolve trade evolutions like Haunter, Kadabra or Machoke?

No trading is needed for the old trade evolutions. They level up while holding an item, often only by day or by night (Haunter holding a Spell Tag at night, for example). Every [Pokémon page](https://originheartgold.github.io/pokemon/) shows how it evolves, and the rules are on [Mechanics and controls](https://originheartgold.github.io/mechanics/#evolution). Some evolutions changed completely: Karrablast and Shelmet simply evolve at Lv. 25. Boldore and Gurdurr still needed a trade in the original hack; from rc6 the English patch evolves them at Lv. 35 (Gigalith) and Lv. 40 (Conkeldurr).

#### My Pokémon didn't learn its evolution move

In the original hack, and in English patches up to rc5, a Pokémon that evolves never learns the moves it should get on evolution (Crobat's Cross Poison, Charizard's Air Slash, Gyarados's Bite and others); only the Move Reminder teaches them. From rc6 the game offers these moves when the Pokémon evolves, each once. For a Pokémon that evolved before you updated, use the Move Reminder.

#### Can other Pokémon Mega Evolve?

No. Charizard is the only Pokémon that can Mega Evolve, holding the Charizardite: Mega Charizard Y with a Timid or Modest nature, Mega Charizard X with any other nature ([held-item forms](https://originheartgold.github.io/mechanics/#held-item-forms)).

#### Where do I get a Light Ball?

- Pikachu starters get one as a [send-off gift in Pallet Town](https://originheartgold.github.io/guide/ch01-first-badge/#pallet-town-send-off-gifts-one-per-starter-before-viridian). Get it before you go to Viridian City.
- Lt. Surge gives one after your Gym battle in Vermilion City (Pikachu starters get a Thunder Stone instead). [After the construction-site clash](https://originheartgold.github.io/guide/ch05-vermilion-thunder/#vermilion-city-after-the-construction-site-clash).
- Wild [Pikachu](https://originheartgold.github.io/pokemon/pikachu/) can hold one.

#### Why can't I use a Full Heal or a Revive in battle?

The original hack leaves most medicine out of the battle Bag: status heals, Full Restore, Max and Hyper Potions, Revives, Ethers and Elixirs. This may be intended. Carry status-healing Berries (Lum, Pecha, Cheri and others) or the Blue, Yellow and Red Flutes, which do work in battle; for PP, the Leppa Berry is in the battle Bag. If you play with the optional difficulty settings, **ITEMS: ALL** (second Options page) adds twenty more medicines to the Trainer-battle Bag; see [Difficulty settings](https://originheartgold.github.io/difficulty/#battle-items-items). The full list is in [Known issues](https://originheartgold.github.io/guide/known-issues/#status-medicine-in-battle).

#### My Pokémon is out of PP and won't use Struggle

In the original hack a Pokémon with no PP left never uses Struggle: FIGHT still opens the move list, and every move says it's out of PP. Switch to another Pokémon, or use a Leppa Berry from the Bag. If your only usable Pokémon has no PP left and you have no Leppa Berry, a Trainer battle can't go on and you have to reset. Watch out in the Route 12 battle against the boyfriend (Ace Trainer Newt), which you have to lose: his Rattata knows only Normal-type moves, so a team of Ghost types can neither lose nor win there. See [Known issues](https://originheartgold.github.io/guide/known-issues/#no-struggle-when-a-pok%C3%A9mon-runs-out-of-pp).

#### Why can't I find a Pokémon or event someone else got?

Many events and some wild Pokémon depend on your starter (Charmander, Pikachu or Bulbasaur). Pick your starter at the top of any quest page and the guide shows only what your game can get.

### Reading references and using the save editor

#### Is every reference entry obtainable or every author claim verified?

No. Entries that cannot be obtained are marked **NOT AVAILABLE IN GAME**. Entries with no known acquisition route are marked separately. Check the Pokémon or item page before planning your team. The [source reference](https://originheartgold.github.io/reference-sources/) explains how the guide’s information was assembled.

#### How do I use the save editor?

Keep a backup, then open your game's battery save in the [save editor](https://originheartgold.github.io/save-editor/). Use a raw **512 KiB `.sav`** or a **DeSmuME `.dsv`** save, not an emulator save state. Follow the editor's controls to make changes and download a copy, then import it through your emulator's save-file controls. Your save is processed locally in your browser.

### Cheats and extras

#### Is there a cheat menu?

The original hack has a built-in Pokémon generator: in the field, **hold SELECT and press X**. Choose the species, level, nature, IVs, held item and more (L and R switch pages), then press **START** to create it. It was made by the Chinese developers, not added by the translation. Whether you use it is up to you. The [save editor](https://originheartgold.github.io/save-editor/) on this site can also change your save.

### About the translation

#### Is the whole game translated?

Yes, from start to end, including the post-game. If you find a mistake, please [report it](https://originheartgold.github.io/contribute/) with a screenshot.

#### Does it have fakemon or changed Pokémon?

No fakemon. The hack does change many Pokémon's stats, abilities, moves and evolutions. Each [Pokémon page](https://originheartgold.github.io/pokemon/) shows the hack's data.

#### How mature is the story?

This fan game contains strong language, sexual themes and innuendo, violence, death, and dark humour. It is intended for mature audiences and is not suitable for children.

The story draws on the Pokémon anime and Pokémon Adventures manga, with the hack's own scenes added. The English translation preserves the original hack's tone and content.

---

## How to use this guide

Source: https://originheartgold.github.io/about/

**The official site of the Origin HeartGold English translation. Patches are published only on our GitHub releases.**

This guide covers **Origin HeartGold (起源心金) v4.0.3** played with the English translation patch.
The game starts in Pallet Town in Kanto. Johto opens up after you become Kanto Champion and finish the story scenes that follow.

### What you need to play

The English translation is a patch: it turns your own copy of **Pokémon HeartGold Version (USA)** into Origin HeartGold in English.
No ROMs are provided here, and the patch only works on that exact version.

The easiest way is the [patcher on this site](https://originheartgold.github.io/patch/): drop in your HeartGold file (the `.nds`, or a `.zip` with it inside) and it checks it, applies the patch published with this site in your browser and gives you the English game. Nothing is uploaded, and you don't need to download the patch yourself. To do it by hand instead:

1. Dump your own HeartGold (USA) cartridge to a `.nds` file. The European, Japanese, Korean and Chinese versions won't work, and neither will a file that's already patched or trimmed.
2. Check the file: its CRC32 must be **C180A0E9**. On Windows, 7-Zip shows it (right-click the file → 7-Zip → CRC SHA → CRC-32). On a Mac, type `crc32 ` in Terminal, drag the file in and press Return; it should print `c180a0e9`. If it doesn't match, the patch will fail or the game will be broken.
3. Download the `.xdelta` patch from the [newest release on GitHub](https://github.com/originheartgold/origin-heart-gold-EN-translation/releases).
4. Apply the patch with an xdelta patcher, for example the in-browser [xdelta-wasm](https://kotcrab.github.io/xdelta-wasm/): choose your HeartGold `.nds` as the source, the `.xdelta` as the patch, apply it and save the new `.nds`. Keep your original file.
5. Play the new `.nds`. The patch is tested in melonDS; other emulators and flashcarts haven't been tested.

### Offline copy

### Pick your game once

Several quests depend on your **starter** (Charmander, Pikachu or Bulbasaur) and on whether you play as a boy or a girl.
At the top of every quest page you can pick both. A quest is hidden only when your game can't get any of it; when just a reward
depends on your starter, the quest stays and its text says so. The choice is remembered in your browser.
Use **Quest type** to show **Main quest** entries (story and badge progression) or **Side quest** entries (optional activities and rewards).
The guide is split into **chapters** in the order the game unlocks things, so early-game and post-game quests are never on the same page.
Each chapter starts with a short walkthrough of where to go next, with the quests that step opens up. A red **Warning** box lists
quests that close for good at that step; it disappears once you have ticked them off (or they don't apply to your game).
The filters combine with your starter and character choices and are remembered between chapters.
You can also tick off quests you've finished and choose **Hide finished** (the ticks are kept per quest, in this browser only).
A quest you follow a direct link to always stays visible.

### How it was made

Quest instructions and configured reference data come from the hack's event scripts, maps, encounter tables and trainer records. Reference pages also include attributed author surveys and supplied English workbooks. Chinese release notes and community reports helped identify questions to check; specific mechanics audits used the original v4.0.3 ROM. Most steps were read from the scripts and have not been checked by playing,
so some still need in-game confirmation, and directions are approximate. Steps checked in an emulator say so; steps that are less certain say "not confirmed in game".
The Pokédex and item pages retain every named entry in the game data. Audited entries without a normal-play route are labelled **NOT AVAILABLE IN GAME**, with the reason on their detail page. They remain useful references for the save editor and the built-in generator (hold SELECT and press X); support for each entry has not been verified. Other entries with no confirmed source remain uncertain rather than being labelled unavailable. If you try something, please [tell us how it went](https://originheartgold.github.io/contribute/).

The [mechanics and controls](https://originheartgold.github.io/mechanics/) page explains the hack’s training and battle changes. [Calendar encounters](https://originheartgold.github.io/calendar/) are listed separately because they appear only on certain dates.

### Reading the evidence

- **Configured data:** a value, table or script record in the game. A stored source does not prove that every story branch can reach it.
- **Game description:** what the English game says. Descriptions and NPC promises can disagree with configured data or behavior.
- **Author note:** an attributed survey or workbook claim. It can describe intent, an older version or an unresolved effect.
- **Tested in game:** a specific documented gameplay test, with its scope stated. It does not certify every use of that mechanic.

Use [move details](https://originheartgold.github.io/moves/), [ability details](https://originheartgold.github.io/abilities/) and the [TM/HM list](https://originheartgold.github.io/tms/) for preparation; [item pages](https://originheartgold.github.io/items/) distinguish acquisition routes from effects and older source notes.

### Known issues

Some quests hit bugs that are in the original Chinese hack. They are listed on the [Known issues](https://originheartgold.github.io/guide/known-issues/) page.
The translation keeps the hack's behaviour as it is and doesn't fix them.

- **[GitHub releases](https://github.com/originheartgold/origin-heart-gold-EN-translation/releases):** the only place we publish the patch. The [GitHub repository](https://github.com/originheartgold/origin-heart-gold-EN-translation) also takes problem reports.
- **[Discord](https://discord.gg/sQY2udrQS):** the official community server, for help and news.
- **[Changelog and contributors](https://originheartgold.github.io/changelog/):** what changed in each release, and who helped.

## Difficulty settings

Source: https://originheartgold.github.io/difficulty/

From **rc7**, the English patch adds three optional difficulty settings: a **level cap** that follows your Gym progress, a switch that turns off **EXP sharing** for benched Pokémon, and a **battle-item limit** for Trainer battles. The original Chinese hack has none of them; they're extras of the English patch. With the level cap off and sharing on, EXP works exactly as in the original hack. The item setting starts on DEFAULT, which keeps the original hack's battle-item rules; ALL adds more medicine (see [Battle items](https://originheartgold.github.io/difficulty/#battle-items-items)). In rc7 this setting was called LIMITED and was stricter than the original hack; rc8 renamed it and gave it the original rules.

### Turning the settings on

1. Open the menu in the field (X) and choose **OPTIONS**.
2. Press **L** or **R**, or tap the arrows at the bottom of the screen, to go to page **2/2**, headed **DIFFICULTY**. Holding **L** while you choose OPTIONS opens this page straight away.
3. Choose a value for each row:
   - **ITEMS:** DEFAULT or ALL (called LIMITED or ALL in rc7).
   - **SHARE:** ON or OFF.
   - **CAP:** OFF or ON.
4. Choose **CONFIRM** to apply your changes (on both Options pages), or **QUIT** or press **B** to throw them away.
5. **Save the game** to keep the settings. Confirming only changes them until you turn the game off; nothing is saved for you.

A new game, and a save from before rc7, starts with **ITEMS DEFAULT, SHARE ON, CAP OFF**. You can change any setting whenever you like outside battle. A battle that has already started keeps the settings and the cap it started with.

### The level cap (CAP)

With **CAP ON**, your Pokémon stop gaining EXP from battles, wild and Trainer alike, once they reach the level of the current cap. The cap depends on which Gyms you've beaten and is shown in the table below.

- **A Pokémon can reach the cap level, but not pass it.** At the cap it gets no more EXP from battles, and the game doesn't show an EXP message for it.
- **EXP over the cap is lost.** It isn't saved for later, and it doesn't go to your other Pokémon. When the cap goes up, a Pokémon starts again from where it stopped.
- **Nothing is taken away.** Pokémon already above the cap (for example one you caught, were given or raised before turning CAP ON) keep their level and EXP, and you can still use them in battle. They just don't gain any more EXP until the cap passes them.
- **EVs are still awarded.** A Pokémon at the cap still gets its EVs from the battle.
- **In battles with a partner,** the cap only applies to your own Pokémon.

#### When the cap goes up

The cap is set by the **first Gym in this list that you haven't beaten yet**. The list follows the order you meet the Gym Leaders in this hack, which starts in Kanto with Brock.

| Next Gym you haven't beaten | Where | Level cap |
|---|---|---:|
| Brock (Boulder Badge) | Pewter City | **12** |
| Misty (Cascade Badge) | Cerulean City | **20** |
| Lt. Surge (Thunder Badge) | Vermilion City | **25** |
| Erika (Rainbow Badge) | Celadon City | **38** |
| Koga (Soul Badge) | Fuchsia City | **55** |
| Blaine (Volcano Badge) | Cinnabar Island | **65** |
| Sabrina (Marsh Badge) | Saffron City | **80** |
| Giovanni (Earth Badge) | Viridian City | **100** |
| Every Johto Gym, and after all Gyms | Johto | **100** |

In practice, **the cap stops limiting you once you've beaten Sabrina** (with every Kanto Gym before her also beaten): from then on it is 100, the normal maximum, for the rest of the game, all through Johto included.

- **The cap goes up after the Gym battle.** The battle against the Gym Leader still uses the old cap, so a Pokémon already at the cap gets no EXP from it. The new cap applies from your next battle.
- **Erika counts as beaten as soon as you win the battle against her in the Celadon Gym.** In this hack she hands over the Rainbow Badge only later, at a ceremony after the [stolen Gloom story](https://originheartgold.github.io/guide/ch08-celadon/#celadon-city-the-stolen-gloom-story-chain-easy-to-get-stuck), but the cap rises to 55 right after your win.
- **The earliest Gym you haven't beaten decides.** Beating a later Gym first doesn't raise the cap past a Gym you skipped. For example, if you start the Saffron City takeover before you've beaten Koga, the cap stays at **55** until you go back and beat him, whatever else you beat in the meantime. Once you beat Koga, the cap jumps straight to the level for the next Gym you still haven't beaten.
- **The cap never goes down.** Beating more Gyms can only keep it the same or raise it.

#### What the cap doesn't limit

- **Rare Candies** still raise a Pokémon's level as normal, even above the cap.
- **The Day Care** still raises the level of the Pokémon you leave there as normal, even above the cap.
- **Some battles aren't affected** by the cap or by the SHARE setting: the Safari Zone, the Bug-Catching Contest, the catching demonstration, battles in the Battle Frontier facilities, link battles with other players, and recorded battles you watch again. They keep the original rules.

### EXP sharing (SHARE)

In the original hack your whole party shares the EXP from every battle: the Pokémon that took part get the full amount, and Pokémon that stayed on the bench get half (see [Mechanics and controls](https://originheartgold.github.io/mechanics/#automatic-exp-and-ev-sharing)).

- **SHARE ON** (the default) keeps that sharing.
- **SHARE OFF** gives **benched Pokémon no EXP and no EVs**, except a Pokémon holding an Exp. Share (see below). Only the Pokémon that took part in the battle gain anything, and each one still gets the same amount as before: switching sharing off doesn't hand the bench's share to the Pokémon that fought.
- A Pokémon **holding an Exp. Share** still shares with SHARE OFF: it gets the same EXP and EVs as it would with SHARE ON, whether or not it took part. The other benched Pokémon get nothing. (In rc7, SHARE OFF also switched the item off; this was fixed in rc8.)
- With **CAP ON** too, the Pokémon that took part, and an Exp. Share holder, still stop at the cap.

### Battle items (ITEMS)

- **DEFAULT** (the default): Trainer battles allow the same Bag items as the original Chinese hack: Berries, the Blue, Yellow and Red Flutes, and also Potion, Super Potion, the drinks, Heal Powder and Berry Juice. Other medicine is left out, as in the original.
- **ALL**: Trainer battles let you use a wider choice of battle items from the Bag, twenty more medicines than DEFAULT, including medicine the original hack doesn't offer in battle (see [Status medicine in battle](https://originheartgold.github.io/guide/known-issues/#status-medicine-in-battle)).

In rc7 the first choice was called **LIMITED** and allowed only Berries and Flutes. That was stricter than the original hack, so rc8 renamed it DEFAULT and restored the original rules. The rule applies to Trainer battles only; the Safari Zone, the Bug-Catching Contest and the other special battles listed above keep their own rules.

Either way, held items, items your opponent uses, wild battles and using items outside battle work as in the original hack.

### Fixed in rc8

Two problems in rc7 are gone in rc8:

- **Story battles you're allowed to lose** (the ones where losing continues the story instead of sending you back to a Pokémon Center) now follow all three settings. In rc7 they ignored CAP and SHARE OFF: every Pokémon got EXP as if CAP were OFF and SHARE were ON, so your Pokémon could pass the cap, and the ITEMS setting did not apply either. Examples: Blue in **Pewter City**, just before Brock's Gym (and his battles in Oak's Lab, Cerulean City and on the S.S. Anne); Misty on Route 3, Red and Green, Bruno in the Pewter City Pokémon Center; several Team Rocket Executive and Giovanni battles, the Celadon Restaurant challengers and the Slowpoke Well battle against Jessie and James. Losing them still continues the story as before.
- **SHARE OFF no longer switches off a held Exp. Share.** The holder shares as with SHARE ON, and everyone else on the bench still gets nothing.

---

## Mechanics and controls

Source: https://originheartgold.github.io/mechanics/

Origin HeartGold adds automatic party training, capture-chain bonuses and new information screens. Here is how to use them in **v4.0.3**.

### Information-screen controls

These are **Nintendo DS buttons**, not particular keyboard keys. Use the corresponding buttons in your emulator or on your controller.

| Where | Button | Action |
|---|---|---|
| Pokémon summary, stats/moves page | **L** | Show IVs and EVs together |
| IV/EV panel | **L or B** | Close the panel |
| Battle command menu | **Y**, or tap the information button at the top right of the touch screen | Open battle information |
| Battle-information panel | **B** | Close the panel |

If the first Y press only highlights a battle command, press Y again. The panel shows information such as stat stages and your Pokémon's ability; it is not a promise that an opponent's unrevealed ability will be visible.

Use **L** for the IV/EV panel with normal button settings; the game’s L/R hint is misleading.

### Automatic EXP and EV sharing

Your party shares battle **experience points (EXP)** and **effort values (EVs)** automatically. EVs are training points that affect a Pokémon's stats; IVs are its individual stat values.

Participating Pokémon receive full EXP; benched Pokémon receive half. Both receive EVs.

The original v4.0.3 hack has **no on/off setting for this sharing**. You do not need the held Exp. Share to enable it. Keep party-wide EV gains in mind when training. From rc7 the English patch adds an optional switch for it, and an optional level cap: see [Difficulty settings](https://originheartgold.github.io/difficulty/). In rc8 a held Exp. Share keeps working with the switch off.

### Capture chains

The [Chain Logger](https://originheartgold.github.io/items/chain-logger/) is added to your Bag during new-game setup. Use it to inspect your chain and the area's encounters.

Catching the same **species and form** builds a chain. The bonuses use the number already caught before the next encounter is generated:

| Completed catches | Hidden Ability selection chance from the chain | Distinct IVs forced to 31 |
|---|---:|---:|
| 0–5 | No chain bonus | 0 |
| 6–9 | 10% | 1 |
| 10–19 | 50% | 2 |
| 20+ | 70% | 4 |

A Pokémon may naturally have more perfect IVs. Hidden Ability selection still depends on that species' ability data.

**The game's displayed ranges are inaccurate around 10 and 20.** The bonus thresholds are 6, 10 and 20 catches. Shiny chances also improve, but the displayed fractions do not establish the exact combined probability; they should not be used as precise odds.

- Catching a different species **or form** starts a new chain at **1**.
- Catching a shiny of the **same species and form** clears the chain.
- A shiny of a **different species or form** follows the new-chain rule and starts at **1**.
- Defeating or fleeing does not advance the chain; they do not reset the chain.

Chain bonuses can apply to a different species from the one you chained, including scripted wild encounters. The chain counter stops increasing at 255.

### EV Allocator

The [EV Allocator](https://originheartgold.github.io/items/ev-allocator/) is added after battle if you do not already have one.

It **redistributes EVs you already earned**. It does not create new training points. Before exiting, you must restore each party member's total to the amount it had when you opened the tool.

| Button | Action |
|---|---|
| Left / Right | Decrease / increase the selected EV by 4 |
| L / R | Decrease / increase it by 64 |
| X / Y | Previous / next party member |
| SELECT | Open the clear-EVs confirmation |
| START | Open the restore-entry-EVs confirmation |

These buttons use the normal button settings.

### Mom's charms

Mom's savings purchases include these three charms. Each purchase is queued for delivery and deducts money from your savings; reaching a threshold does not mean immediate receipt.

| Charm | Savings threshold | Cost from savings |
|---|---:|---:|
| [Catching Charm](https://originheartgold.github.io/items/catching-charm/) | $30,000 | $3,000 |
| [Exp. Charm](https://originheartgold.github.io/items/exp-charm/) | $40,000 | $3,000 |
| [Shiny Charm](https://originheartgold.github.io/items/shiny-charm/) | $50,000 | $3,000 |

**There is no Oval Charm** in this game: it is unavailable.

### Visible encounters and shinies

The game supports up to **six visible wild Pokémon** nearby. Repel prevents new visible spawns. Visible Pokémon can also reduce ordinary encounters nearby.

A visible shiny has a sparkle and sound cue. The game keeps **one visible shiny** and can use it when you re-enter the same map, searching for a position near you. Terrain can still prevent an accessible placement, and another shiny can replace the single record.

**Catch a visible shiny before restarting.** Restarting clears it. Do not rely on an ordinary save to preserve it for later.

Special [calendar encounters](https://originheartgold.github.io/calendar/) modify particular land encounters on annual dates. They are listed separately from the ordinary location tables.

### Evolution

The hack rewrites many evolutions. Each [Pokémon](https://originheartgold.github.io/pokemon/) page lists its evolution requirements. The main rules:

- **No trading needed for the old trade evolutions.** Kadabra, Machoke, Graveler, Haunter and the rest now evolve when they level up holding an item, often only by day or by night (for example Haunter → Gengar holding a Spell Tag at night, Machoke → Machamp holding a Black Belt by day). Onix and Porygon simply level up. Boldore and Gurdurr still need a trade in the original hack; the English patch from rc6 evolves them at Lv. 35 and Lv. 40 instead.
- **Evolution moves:** from rc6 the English patch offers a Pokémon its evolution moves when it evolves (Crobat's Cross Poison, for example), each once. In the original hack only the Move Reminder teaches them.
- **Day and night:** night is 20:00–3:59, "day" is 4:00–19:59. A few evolutions need 10:00–16:59 and say so.
- **Friendship:** "high friendship" means 220 or more; Sylveon needs 158 or more plus a Fairy-type move.
- **The first match wins:** Meowth, Slowpoke and Cubone must take their held-item evolution before the level of their normal one, and Eevee checks Sylveon and Espeon before Glaceon.
- **Some evolutions can't happen:** a few evolution methods do not work. Most belong to Pokémon that can't be met anyway; the ones that matter are Moss Rock Leafeon and magnetic-field Probopass, which still evolve with a Leaf Stone or Thunder Stone. See [Known issues](https://originheartgold.github.io/guide/known-issues/#evolutions-that-cannot-happen).

### Held-item forms

Use the [move reference](https://originheartgold.github.io/moves/) for stats, effects and learning methods, and the [ability reference](https://originheartgold.github.io/abilities/) to find abilities for your team. The [TM/HM list](https://originheartgold.github.io/tms/) shows where to get each machine and which Pokémon can use it.

### Pickup

A Pokémon with [Pickup](https://originheartgold.github.io/abilities/pickup/) can find items after battle. Items go straight into the Bag; the Pokémon does not need an empty held-item slot. Eggs do not activate Pickup.

**Pickup first has a 10% chance to activate per eligible check.** The chart then gives each item's chance **after activation**. For example, a **30%** entry means approximately **3% per eligible check**; a **1%** entry means approximately **0.1%**. These are nominal chances, not guaranteed rewards after a fixed number of battles.

### Other training and battle changes

- **Held items after battle:** the game restores many items, but has exceptions, including special berry handling. Do not assume every consumed, stolen or knocked-off item comes back.
- **Hatching:** Flame Body and Magma Armor speed up hatching. Their effects do not stack with multiple holders. See [Overworld abilities](https://originheartgold.github.io/overworld-abilities/) for every ability that works outside battle, and [Apricorn trees](https://originheartgold.github.io/apricorn-trees/) for where to pick each colour.
- **Destiny Knot:** either parent holding it raises inherited IV slots to five. This does not guarantee five perfect IVs.
- **Everstone:** give it to one parent to pass on its nature. Using two holders or parents from different language games can affect inheritance.

### Field moves

The hack intentionally lets you use scripted obstacle moves without teaching them to a Pokémon. Badge requirements still apply, and party-menu moves have separate restrictions. See the [field-move table](https://originheartgold.github.io/guide/ch01-first-badge/#field-moves-which-badge-each-one-needs) for the precise distinctions.

---

## Origin HeartGold walkthrough and quest guide

Source: https://originheartgold.github.io/guide/

Main quests, side quests, puzzles and easy-to-miss events in Origin HeartGold (起源心金 v4.0.3), in the order the game unlocks them, chapter by chapter.

The quest instructions are based on the game's event scripts, maps, trainers and wild Pokémon tables, with specific audit findings noted beside the affected steps. Steps that were checked in an emulator say so; most others have not been played through. The English patch doesn't change what happens in quests, so what's described is how the original Chinese hack behaves. Directions are approximate, and steps marked "not confirmed in game" have not been checked by playing. The game starts in Pallet Town in Kanto. Johto opens up after you become Kanto Champion and finish the story scenes that follow (see [Pokémon League, Mt. Silver and New Bark Town](https://originheartgold.github.io/guide/ch14-cerulean-cave-mt-silver-lodge/)).

Several quests depend on your **starter** (Charmander, Pikachu or Bulbasaur), gender, the weekday, or earlier choices. Each entry says so in its title or under **Who gets it**. "Post-game" in this guide means after your **final** Hall of Fame entry; things that open after your first one say so.

On the website, every entry has a **Main quest** or **Side quest** tag. Main quests cover story and badge progression, including conditional story routes and walkthroughs; side quests cover optional activities and rewards. **Post-game** tags mark entries that open only after the final Hall of Fame. Use **Quest type** at the top of each chapter to filter them alongside your starter, character and finished quests. Your filters are remembered between chapters, and a quest you follow a direct link to always stays visible.

The website also has [moves](https://originheartgold.github.io/moves/), [abilities](https://originheartgold.github.io/abilities/), [TMs and HMs](https://originheartgold.github.io/tms/) and [items](https://originheartgold.github.io/items/). Their evidence labels separate configured game data, in-game text, attributed author notes and specific gameplay tests. [Reference sources](https://originheartgold.github.io/reference-sources/) explains coverage and conflicts; an author note or matching data does not prove an event can be reached.

### Chapters

Each chapter says where to go next (the main quest), which quests it opens up, and which ones it closes for good. Post-game chapters come last. The chapters are listed on the website; on GitHub they are the files in `guide/chapters/`, and the quest entries themselves are in the numbered files beside this one.

- [Chapter 1: The First Badge](https://originheartgold.github.io/guide/ch01-first-badge/): Pallet Town to Pewter City and Brock's Boulder Badge. (17)
- [Chapter 2: Mt. Moon](https://originheartgold.github.io/guide/ch02-mt-moon/): Route 3 and Mt. Moon: gather your four companions and get past the fake construction guards. (7)
- [Chapter 3: Cerulean City and the Cascade Badge](https://originheartgold.github.io/guide/ch03-cerulean-cascade/): Cerulean City, the Cape Battle Festival, Bill's cottage and Misty's Cascade Badge. (4)
- [Chapter 4: Past the Cascade Badge](https://originheartgold.github.io/guide/ch04-underground-path/): Mt. Moon Square revisited, Route 9 and 10, the Route 5 shelter and the Underground Path to Vermilion. (7)
- [Chapter 5: Vermilion City and the Thunder Badge](https://originheartgold.github.io/guide/ch05-vermilion-thunder/): The construction-site dispute, Lt. Surge's Thunder Badge and everything Vermilion opens up. (12)
- [Chapter 6: The S.S. Anne](https://originheartgold.github.io/guide/ch06-ss-anne/): The party on board, the Team Rocket hijack and the one chance to save the ship. (3)
- [Chapter 7: Rock Tunnel and Lavender Town](https://originheartgold.github.io/guide/ch07-rock-tunnel-lavender/): Rescue Prof. Hale in Rock Tunnel, then Lavender Town and the haunted Pokémon Tower. (15)
- [Chapter 8: Saffron City and Celadon City](https://originheartgold.github.io/guide/ch08-celadon/): Through Saffron City to Route 7, the Team Rocket hideout under Celadon and the Rainbow Badge. (20)
- [Chapter 9: Cycling Road, Fuchsia City and the Soul Badge](https://originheartgold.github.io/guide/ch09-fuchsia-soul-badge/): The Secret Potion run down Cycling Road, Koga's ninja trial in Fuchsia and the Soul Badge. (16)
- [Chapter 10: Surf to Cinnabar Island and the Volcano Badge](https://originheartgold.github.io/guide/ch10-cinnabar-volcano-badge/): Surf south past Seafoam Islands to Cinnabar Island, Blaine's hidden Gym and the Detrick lab where Mewtwo breaks loose. (8)
- [Chapter 11: Pokémon Tower, the Saffron Takeover and the Marsh Badge](https://originheartgold.github.io/guide/ch11-saffron-takeover-marsh-badge/): Make Sabrina laugh in Pokémon Tower, take back Saffron City from Team Rocket and win the Marsh Badge. (7)
- [Chapter 12: The Alto Mare Islands, Viridian Gym and the Earth Badge](https://originheartgold.github.io/guide/ch12-alto-mare-viridian-earth-badge/): Granny Mae's trial on Two Island reopens the Viridian Gym; Giovanni's Earth Badge is the last Kanto Badge. (22)
- [Chapter 13: Victory Road and the Indigo Conference](https://originheartgold.github.io/guide/ch13-victory-road-indigo-conference/): The qualifiers on Victory Road, the Indigo Conference tournament and the Elite Four, ending in your first Hall of Fame. (4)
- [Chapter 14: Cerulean Cave and the Mt. Silver Lodge](https://originheartgold.github.io/guide/ch14-cerulean-cave-mt-silver-lodge/): After your first Hall of Fame entry: Giovanni's duel in Cerulean Cave, your rehabilitation at the Mt. Silver lodge and Prof. Oak's errand that opens Johto. (5)
- [Chapter 15: Into Johto: Route 26, Route 27 and New Bark Town](https://originheartgold.github.io/guide/ch15-route-26-new-bark-town/): Walk south from the Indigo Plateau gate to Route 27 and New Bark Town and deliver Prof. Oak's Pokédexes to Prof. Elm. (7)
- [Chapter 16: Route 29, Cherrygrove City and the Dark Cave](https://originheartgold.github.io/guide/ch16-cherrygrove-dark-cave/): Crystal's tour of Cherrygrove City, Route 30 and 31, and Team Rocket's dig at the other end of Dark Cave. (11)
- [Chapter 17: Violet City, Sprout Tower and the Zephyr Badge](https://originheartgold.github.io/guide/ch17-violet-city-sprout-tower/): Violet City, the memorial ceremony in Sprout Tower and Falkner's Flying-type Gym. (13)
- [Chapter 18: The Ruins of Alph, Route 32 and Union Cave](https://originheartgold.github.io/guide/ch18-ruins-of-alph-union-cave/): Find the missing Molly in the Ruins of Alph, then follow Route 32 and Union Cave south to Route 33. (15)
- [Chapter 19: Azalea Town, Slowpoke Well and Ilex Forest](https://originheartgold.github.io/guide/ch19-azalea-slowpoke-well-ilex-forest/): Team Rocket goes after the Tidal Bell in Slowpoke Well, Bugsy needs help in Ilex Forest, and you win the Hive Badge. (9)
- [Chapter 20: Route 34, Goldenrod City and the Plain Badge](https://originheartgold.github.io/guide/ch20-route-34-goldenrod-city/): Route 34 and the big city of Goldenrod: the Radio Tower recording, Whitney's Gym and a long list of city jobs. (20)
- [Chapter 21: Routes 35 to 37, the National Park and Silver on Route 37](https://originheartgold.github.io/guide/ch21-routes-35-37-national-park/): North of Goldenrod: the National Park, the odd tree on Route 36 and the first rematch scene with Silver on Route 37. (10)
- [Chapter 22: Ecruteak City, the Burned Tower and the Fog Badge](https://originheartgold.github.io/guide/ch22-ecruteak-burned-tower-fog-badge/): The Marauder at the Burned Tower, the Bell Tower gate quiz, Morty's Ghost Gym and Ecruteak's small errands. (10)
- [Chapter 23: Routes 38 and 39, Olivine City and the Mineral Badge](https://originheartgold.github.io/guide/ch23-route-39-olivine-mineral-badge/): West from Ecruteak: MooMoo Farm, Gold and Crystal on Route 39, Olivine City, Jasmine's Steel Gym and Team Rocket in the Lighthouse. (19)
- [Chapter 24: Cianwood City, Cianwood Cave and the Storm Badge](https://originheartgold.github.io/guide/ch24-cianwood-city-storm-badge/): The Secret Potion for Amphy, Chuck in Cianwood Cave, the Raikou device on Route 47 and the Storm Badge. (20)
- [Chapter 25: Route 42, Mt. Mortar and the Lake of Rage](https://originheartgold.github.io/guide/ch25-route-42-mt-mortar-lake-of-rage/): Silver and a brainwashed Entei on Route 42, the Mt. Mortar expedition, Mahogany Town and the red Gyarados at the Lake of Rage. (8)
- [Chapter 26: Mahogany Town, the Team Rocket HQ and the Glacier Badge](https://originheartgold.github.io/guide/ch26-mahogany-rocket-hq-glacier-badge/): The souvenir shop that hides a Rocket base, the Boot Camp Ruins, the HQ's three floors and Pryce's no-weather Gym. (6)
- [Chapter 27: Route 44, the Ice Path, Blackthorn City and the Rising Badge](https://originheartgold.github.io/guide/ch27-ice-path-blackthorn-rising-badge/): East from Mahogany through the Ice Path, Clair's dragon rule and the Dragon's Den: the eighth and last Johto Badge. (14)
- [Chapter 28: The Silver Conference and the League HQ's First Round](https://originheartgold.github.io/guide/ch28-silver-conference-hq-round-1/): Giovanni on Mt. Silver, the Silver Conference at the summit and the first leads from the Trainer Affairs desk. (5)
- [Chapter 29: League HQ Rounds 2 and 3](https://originheartgold.github.io/guide/ch29-hq-rounds-2-and-3/): Seafoam Islands and Kyogre, then Violet City's stolen Jade Orb, the Forest of Time, the legendary tracks in Johto and the sick Miltank at MooMoo Farm. (6)
- [Chapter 30: League HQ Round 4](https://originheartgold.github.io/guide/ch30-hq-round-4/): Ho-Oh stolen from the Bell Tower, Lugia at the Whirl Islands, Giovanni's chase from Dark Cave to Dialga's and Palkia's spaces, and Petrel at the Lake of Rage. (7)
- [Chapter 31: The Island Pilgrimage](https://originheartgold.github.io/guide/ch31-island-pilgrimage/): Sign up on Seven Island, clear the trials of all six islands, then follow Team Rocket from the Ritual Shrine to the Ruins of Alph. (15)
- [Chapter 32: The Final March and the Final Hall of Fame](https://originheartgold.github.io/guide/ch32-final-march-hall-of-fame/): Team Rocket's all-out war: the Radio Tower broadcast, Victory Road, Mewtwo, the Elite Four rooms and Giovanni in the Hall of Fame. (7)
- [Chapter 33: Postgame, Lance's Visit and the Seized Items](https://originheartgold.github.io/guide/ch33-postgame-lances-visit-seized-items/): Back home after the final Hall of Fame: Lance returns the legendary items, and the orbs open the legendary encounters across Kanto, the Sevii Islands and Sinjoh Ruins. (9)
- [Chapter 34: Postgame, the Legends of Johto](https://originheartgold.github.io/guide/ch34-postgame-johto-legends/): The three beasts, Ho-Oh and Lugia, the Griseous Orb, the Battle Frontier's stone and the dreams of Cresselia and Darkrai. (10)

- [Hidden items](https://originheartgold.github.io/guide/hidden-items/): every hidden item with a screenshot of where to stand and press A.
- [Known issues](https://originheartgold.github.io/guide/known-issues/): suspected bugs in the original hack that affect quests (reported, not fixed).

### Start here

- [Romance route: how it's unlocked, how your partner is chosen, and what locks a partner out (central entry)](https://originheartgold.github.io/guide/ch20-route-34-goldenrod-city/#romance-route-how-its-unlocked-how-your-partner-is-chosen-and-what-locks-a-partner-out-central-entry)
